name: Connect Navimow
description: >-
  use this when the user needs to connect a Segway Navimow robot mower, sign in,
  finish first-run setup, or re-authenticate

# Connect a Segway Navimow

Walk the user through connecting their Navimow account so this bot can send commands. Keep it conversational. One step at a time.

There is no Navimow connector in the catalog. Control goes through Segway's official `navimow-sdk` on this computer (cloud API at `https://navimow-fra.ninebot.com`). Home Assistant is an optional fallback if they already run it.

## Passwords and tokens: Vault only

- Never ask for a password, 2FA code, or token in chat. If they paste one anyway, use it once and keep it out of replies.
- Never write a password, access token, refresh token, or client secret to a file on this computer, to memory, to a skill, or to a routine. No credentials file.
- The login goes in the user's Grok Bot Vault through the Secure Form. The Vault fills it into the Navimow sign-in page without the bot ever seeing the password.
- An access token lives only in memory of the one script that uses it. Do not save it. When a token is missing or expired, sign in again from the Vault login and finish the command in the same script.

## First step: ask about the Vault

Before asking for any login, check Vault list with kind login for a Navimow login. If one exists, use it and skip to sign-in.

If none exists, send ONE question widget: "Save your Navimow login in your Grok Bot Vault so I can sign you back in later?" Options: "Yes, save it to my Vault (recommended)" and "No, just use it this once". Wait for the answer.

Then send the Secure Form (kind login, site from the live Navimow sign-in page, prefill the email if they gave it). Pass choice "save" for yes and "use_once" for no. Tell them in one line that the password is stored encrypted and filled in only when needed, and that you never see it.

## Direct sign-in (default)

1. `pip install -U navimow-sdk` (Python 3.11+).
2. Fetch OAuth constants live from the official Home Assistant integration. Do not invent them and do not copy them into memory: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/segwaynavimow/NavimowHA/main/custom_components/navimow/const.py`. You need `OAUTH2_AUTHORIZE`, `OAUTH2_TOKEN`, `CLIENT_ID`, `CLIENT_SECRET`, `API_BASE_URL`.
3. Start a short-lived local callback on this computer to capture `?code=`.
4. Open the authorize URL in the computer's browser with `channel=homeassistant` and a `redirect_uri` pointing at that callback.
5. Sign in on that page with the Vault login (the browser task fills the Vault references; it never types the password itself). If a one-time code or captcha blocks it, hand the screen to the user.
6. When the callback gets `code`, POST it to `OAUTH2_TOKEN` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`: `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `redirect_uri`. Keep the returned token in memory only.
7. Discover mowers with `MowerAPI.async_get_devices()` and send one status read to prove it works.
8. Remember only non-secret facts: mower display name, model, and that Navimow is connected.

If several mowers come back, ask which one is default with a question widget listing the real names.

## If OAuth redirect fails

Navimow's published OAuth client is built for Home Assistant, so a custom redirect can be rejected. Say that plainly, then offer Home Assistant as the fallback. Do not scrape cookies or reuse a session to get around it.

## Home Assistant fallback

Only if they already have Home Assistant, or direct sign-in failed.

1. They install the official integration: HACS custom repo `https://github.com/segwaynavimow/NavimowHA`, then add the Navimow integration and sign in there.
2. They enable Home Assistant's Model Context Protocol Server integration.
3. Add Home Assistant's `/api/mcp` as a connector and sign in with the connect card so no token is pasted. If the card cannot sign in and a long-lived access token is the only option, collect it with a masked secret request, never in chat, and never in a file.
4. Control the `lawn_mower` entity after that.

## Done

Tell them they can say start mowing, pause, go home, or how's the battery.

---
name: Control Navimow
description: >-
  use this when the user wants to start, pause, resume, dock, stop, or check
  status of a Segway Navimow robot lawn mower
---
# Control a Segway Navimow

Use this whenever the user wants the mower to do something, or asks how it is doing. If no Navimow login is saved in the Vault, or sign-in fails, run Connect Navimow first.

## Safety

This moves a real machine with spinning blades.

- Start or resume: confirm with a question widget first ("Start mowing? Lawn clear of people and pets?"). Do not send the command until they confirm. Refuse if status is error, rain, lifted, or battery is too low to mow, and say why.
- Pause, stop, or dock: do it immediately. No confirmation.
- Never send a command you cannot map to `MowerCommand`. Never invent a zone, schedule, or cutting-height call unless the installed SDK exposes it.

## Credentials

No credentials file exists and none should be created. Tokens stay in memory of the script that uses them. To get a fresh token, sign in from the user's Vault login as Connect Navimow describes, then run the command in the same script and discard the token. Never print or save a token.

## Talk to the mower

Install the official SDK: `pip install -U navimow-sdk`.

```python
import aiohttp
from mower_sdk.api import MowerAPI
from mower_sdk.models import MowerCommand

API_BASE = "https://navimow-fra.ninebot.com"

async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
    api = MowerAPI(session, token, API_BASE)
    devices = await api.async_get_devices()
    status = await api.async_get_device_status(device_id)
    await api.async_send_command(device_id, command)
```

| User said | Enum |
| --- | --- |
| start / mow / go | `MowerCommand.START` |
| pause | `MowerCommand.PAUSE` |
| resume / keep going | `MowerCommand.RESUME` |
| go home / dock / charge | `MowerCommand.DOCK` |
| stop | `MowerCommand.STOP` |

`alreadyInState` from the API counts as success. After a command, re-read status and report the new state in plain language plus battery percent.

If they have more than one mower and did not name one, ask with a widget of the real names.

## Status

For how's it doing, battery, or where is it: `async_get_device_status`. Reply in one or two short sentences with state, battery, and any error. Typical states: idle, mowing, paused, docked, charging, returning, error.

## Home Assistant path

If they connected Home Assistant instead of the SDK, call the `lawn_mower` entity (start, pause, dock) and read its battery sensor. Same safety rules.

## Token expiry

On 401 or `CODE_OAUTH_INFO_ILLEGAL`, sign in again from the Vault login once. If that fails, run Connect Navimow. Do not loop commands.

  setup, or re-authenticate
---
# Connect a Matic robot vacuum

Walk the user through connecting their Matic so this bot can send commands. Keep it conversational. One step at a time. Never ask them to paste a password, 2FA code, or token into chat.

There is no Matic connector in the catalog and no consumer cloud API. Matic's official control path is Matter, via Home Assistant, Apple Home, or Google Home. This bot cannot reach the robot on the user's Wi-Fi by itself, so Home Assistant is the way in.

Do not use unofficial SDKs, reverse-engineered local protocols, community Bluetooth pairing, or app scraping.

## Passwords and tokens: Vault only

Never write a password or token to a file on this computer, to memory, to a skill, or to a routine. Logins go in the user's Grok Bot Vault through the Secure Form. If Home Assistant needs a sign-in, check Vault list for it first. If none is saved, ask ONE question widget: "Save your Home Assistant login in your Grok Bot Vault?" with "Yes, save it (recommended)" and "No, just this once", then send the Secure Form with choice "save" or "use_once" to match.

## Prefer an existing Home Assistant connector

If Home Assistant is already connected (for example from Navimow setup), reuse it. Check connector status, find the vacuum entity, and skip adding a second server.

## Official path: Home Assistant + Matter

1. In the Matic app: Settings, Connectivity, Connect to Smart Home App, Enter Pairing Mode, then pick Home Assistant. Official guide: https://support.maticrobots.com/how-to-connect-matic-to-home-assistant
2. They need Matic on Wi-Fi and IPv6 enabled on the home network, Home Assistant, and Matic. IPv6 off is the usual reason pairing looks fine and then control dies.
3. They enable Home Assistant's built-in Model Context Protocol Server integration.
4. Add Home Assistant's `/api/mcp` as a connector and sign in with its connect card so no token is pasted. If the card cannot sign in and a long-lived access token is the only option, collect it with a masked secret request, never in chat, and never in a file.
5. Confirm a `vacuum.*` entity exists. Optionally they can map Matic rooms to Home Assistant areas (entity settings, Map vacuum segments to areas) so clean the kitchen works.
6. Remember only non-secret facts: that Matic is connected, the vacuum's display name, and that control is through Home Assistant.

## If they do not have Home Assistant

Say so plainly: Matic is local Matter, so this bot needs Home Assistant as the bridge. Do not offer unofficial workarounds.

## Done

Tell them they can say start cleaning, clean the kitchen, pause, go home, or is Matic docked.

---
name: Control Matic
description: >-
  use this when the user wants to start, pause, dock, stop, clean a room, or
  check status of a Matic robot vacuum
---
# Control a Matic robot vacuum

Use this whenever the user wants the Matic vacuum to do something, or asks how it is doing. If Home Assistant is not connected or no vacuum entity is visible, run Connect Matic first.

## Safety

This moves a real robot around the house.

- Start cleaning or clean a room: confirm with a question widget first that floors are clear of pets, cables, and small objects. Do not send the command until they confirm. Refuse if the vacuum is in `error` or unavailable; say why.
- Pause, stop, or dock / return home: do it immediately. These are the safe actions. No confirmation.

## Talk to the vacuum

Control the Home Assistant `vacuum.*` entity for Matic.

| User said | HA action |
| --- | --- |
| start / clean / vacuum | `vacuum.start` |
| pause | `vacuum.pause` |
| stop | `vacuum.stop` |
| go home / dock / charge | `vacuum.return_to_base` |
| find it / locate | `vacuum.locate` |
| clean the kitchen (or other room) | `vacuum.clean_area` with mapped areas |

For a room name, use `vacuum.clean_area` only if segments are mapped to Home Assistant areas. If mapping is missing, say they need to map rooms in the vacuum entity settings, and offer a whole-home start instead.

After a command, re-read state and reply in one or two short sentences: cleaning, paused, docked, returning, idle, or error.

If they have more than one vacuum and did not name one, ask with a widget of the real names. If they also have a Navimow, do not send mower commands when they meant the vacuum.

## Status

For how's Matic, is it docked, battery: read the vacuum entity and any battery sensor. Do not dump raw JSON.

Typical states: `cleaning`, `docked`, `idle`, `paused`, `returning`, `error`.

## Token / connection errors

If the Home Assistant connector needs auth or the vacuum entity disappears, re-run Connect Matic. Do not loop commands.

---
# Connect a home robot

Use this when the user wants to add a robot vacuum, mower, mop, or other home robot that is not covered by Connect Navimow or Connect Matic. A Segway Navimow uses Connect Navimow. A Matic vacuum uses Connect Matic.

Keep it conversational. Ask the brand and what it is (vacuum, mower, mop, other) if they did not say. Never ask them to paste a password, 2FA code, or token into chat.

## Passwords and tokens: Vault only

Never write a password or token to a file on this computer, to memory, to a skill, or to a routine. Logins go in the user's Grok Bot Vault through the Secure Form. Before asking for any login, check Vault list. If none is saved, ask ONE question widget: "Save this login in your Grok Bot Vault?" with "Yes, save it (recommended)" and "No, just this once", then send the Secure Form with choice "save" or "use_once" to match. The Vault fills the login into the page without the bot ever seeing the password.

## Official only

Use only:

1. A catalog connector for that brand, if SearchPlugins finds a real one.
2. Home Assistant's core, official integration for that brand (docs on home-assistant.io), including Matter.
3. The vendor's own documented cloud SDK or Open API.

Do not use unofficial HACS repos, reverse-engineered local protocols, community Bluetooth pairing, cookie scraping, or app scraping. If the only known path is unofficial, say so and stop.

## Prefer an existing Home Assistant connector

If Home Assistant is already connected, reuse it and help them add the official integration for that brand inside it.

## How to connect

1. SearchPlugins for the brand. If a real connector exists, confirm with a question widget, then install and authenticate it.
2. Otherwise look up the official Home Assistant integration on home-assistant.io (official examples: `roborock`, `roomba`, `husqvarna_automower`, `matter`). Confirm it is a core integration page, not a GitHub fork.
3. Walk them through that official setup: the vendor app account, Matter pairing from the robot's own app, or the vendor's documented OAuth.
4. If they do not have Home Assistant and the device is local Matter or Home Assistant only, say they need it as the bridge.
5. Enable Home Assistant's Model Context Protocol Server if needed. Add `/api/mcp` as a connector and sign in with its connect card so no token is pasted. If a long-lived token is the only option, collect it with a masked secret request, never in chat, and never in a file.
6. Confirm the entity exists (`vacuum.*`, `lawn_mower.*`, or the official domain).
7. Remember only non-secret facts: brand, type, display name, and how it is connected.

If several matching devices appear, ask which one with a widget of the real names.

## Done

Tell them they can say start, pause, go home, clean a named room if mapped, or how's it doing.

# Control a home robot

Use this when the user wants to start, pause, dock, stop, clean a room, or check status of a connected home robot that is not a Navimow or Matic. If it is a Segway Navimow, run Control Navimow. If it is a Matic, run Control Matic. If nothing is connected for that brand, run Connect home robot first.

## Safety

These are real moving machines.

- Mower start/resume: confirm the lawn is clear of people and pets.
- Vacuum/mop start or clean a room: confirm floors are clear of pets, cables, and small objects.
- Other robots that move: confirm the area is clear of people and pets.
- Pause, stop, or dock / return home: do it immediately. No confirmation.
- Refuse if the entity is `error` or unavailable; say why.
- Never send a command the official integration does not expose. Never use unofficial tools.

## Talk to the robot

Prefer the existing Home Assistant connector.

Vacuums (`vacuum.*`):

| User said | HA action |
| --- | --- |
| start / clean | `vacuum.start` |
| pause | `vacuum.pause` |
| stop | `vacuum.stop` |
| go home / dock | `vacuum.return_to_base` |
| find it | `vacuum.locate` |
| clean a named room | `vacuum.clean_area` if rooms are mapped |

Mowers (`lawn_mower.*`):

| User said | HA action |
| --- | --- |
| start / mow | `lawn_mower.start_mowing` |
| pause | `lawn_mower.pause` |
| go home / dock | `lawn_mower.dock` |

If they named a brand with an official catalog connector or vendor SDK, use that instead of guessing HA action names. Look up the live tool schema first.

If several robots could match, ask with a widget of the real names. Do not send a mower command when they meant a vacuum, or the reverse.

After a command, re-read state and reply in one or two short sentences plus battery if you have it.

## Status

Read the entity and battery sensor. Do not dump raw JSON. Typical vacuum states: cleaning, docked, idle, paused, returning, error. Typical mower states: mowing, paused, docked, returning, error.

## Connection errors

If the connector needs auth or the entity disappears, re-run the matching Connect skill. Do not loop commands.

# Share this home-robots bot

When the owner wants copy they can send to other people, give them a short note they can paste. Do not dump setup internals or secrets.

## What to send

1. Open the template link and import the bot.
2. Tell it which robots they have (Navimow, Matic, Roborock, Roomba, Husqvarna, or anything else).
3. When it asks, choose whether to save your login in your Grok Bot Vault. Yes is recommended. Your password is stored encrypted there and the bot never sees it.
4. Navimow: sign in with the same account used in the Navimow app.
5. Matic and most other home robots: pair through official Home Assistant or Matter from the robot's own app, then let the bot connect to that Home Assistant.
6. Confirm the devices it finds.
7. Talk in plain language: start mowing, start cleaning, clean the kitchen, pause, go home, how's the battery.

Mention that start or clean will ask them to confirm people, pets, and floors are clear.

## Official only

The bot uses official vendor apps, official Home Assistant integrations, and Matter. It will not use unofficial hacks. Recipients need Home Assistant for Matic and for most other local or Matter robots. Navimow can sign in directly. If they already use Home Assistant, one connection can cover every robot it already sees.

## What not to send

No client secrets, tokens, passwords, device ids, or file paths.
